thread:
Marissa Cole: ok team, need a decision today on which console nudges graduate to “always-on” onboarding vs stay behind flags for iteration. want to lock before we write final sprint readout.

Marissa Cole: current set in experiment (week 2):
1) “Create an API key” (shows on Overview if no key)
2) “Make your first request” (shows after key created, no first_success)
3) “Enable streaming” (after first request, streaming=false)
4) “View usage dashboard” (after first_success)
5) “Set usage alerts / budget” (after first_success)

Marissa Cole: proposal from me: 1 + 2 always-on, 3/4 behind flag, 5 kill for now. thoughts?

Dylan Brooks: +1 to 1/2 always-on. those are basically “can’t proceed without it” steps and they’re stable now.

Dylan Brooks: reminder we fixed the earlier issue where the API key nudge state could block the create key flow (SUP-24905). don’t want to reintroduce anything risky.

Kenji Nakamura: design-wise, 1/2 are the cleanest and least “marketing-y”. 3 is still a little confusing copy-wise (“streaming” doesn’t land for some folks).

Kenji Nakamura: for 4 (usage dashboard) the placement is good but the CTA label needs work. current “View dashboard” looks like a detour vs “See your token usage”.

Ben Carter: sharing the metrics snippet from week 2 readout (rough):
- Nudge #1 CTR ~22%, completion (api_key_created) up ~7% absolute vs holdout
- Nudge #2 CTR ~18%, completion (first_successful_request) up ~4–5% absolute
- Nudge #3 CTR ~6%, streaming_enabled event is noisy + low baseline
- Nudge #4 CTR ~9%, dashboard_viewed up but unclear if it drives retention
- Nudge #5 CTR ~3% and we saw a few “what is this” comments in #support

Ben Carter: net: 1/2 show clear activation lift. others are “nice to have” / education.

Paula Mendes: from telemetry perspective, 1/2 also have the cleanest event mapping and least ambiguity.

Paula Mendes: 3 is tricky because streaming can be enabled via SDK defaults (or not applicable) and we’re not reliably catching it everywhere yet.

Logan Wright: +1. if we make 3 always-on before we’re confident in event coverage, we’ll spend cycles arguing with dashboards.

Soojin Lee: messaging lens: keep always-on nudges focused on “get to first value fast”. 1/2 fit.

Soojin Lee: 3 can be framed as “faster responses” but it’s not essential to first value.

Leila Farouk: QA note: 1/2 are stable across routes (Overview + API Keys + Quickstart). 3/4/5 have more edge cases depending on which console page you land on first.

Leila Farouk: also dismissal persistence for 3 is still inconsistent if you switch orgs (seen once in staging). not a blocker if it stays flagged.

Nikhil Sharma: product POV: always-on should be “minimal onboarding checklist”. if it’s >2–3 items, it starts feeling like nagging.

Marissa Cole: ok sounds aligned. question: do we want to keep “usage dashboard” (#4) at all, or just park it?

Ben Carter: I’d keep it behind flag + iterate. it’s a decent moment to explain cost visibility (token breakdown) which is part of our value prop.

Soojin Lee: agree but copy needs to be crisp + not guilt-y. “Track token usage and latency” vs “See dashboard”.

Kenji Nakamura: I can do a copy pass today. suggestion:
- Title: “See what your first request cost”
- Body: “Token + latency breakdowns help you optimize quickly.”
- CTA: “Open usage”

Dylan Brooks: if we keep #4 flagged, we can target it to only show after first_success + at least 10k tokens, so it’s not immediately after hello world.

Paula Mendes: +1. we can avoid showing it for super-light testers. also reduces noise for people who bounce.

Jada Williams: flag mechanics: we currently have `lg_console_nudges_v1` w/ cohort assignment and holdout. we can add sub-flags per nudge or use config list. prefer config list so we don’t explode flags.

Marissa Cole: config list is fine. do we agree on:
- always-on: nudge_api_key, nudge_first_request
- iterate behind flag: nudge_usage_dashboard (with new targeting)
- keep behind flag (optional): nudge_streaming (copy + instrumentation work)
- kill: nudge_alerts

Dylan Brooks: yes.

Ben Carter: yes. for final readout we’ll call out that 1/2 “graduated to always-on onboarding checklist” and 3/4 stay experimental.

Logan Wright: please keep tracking on 1/2 even if always-on. we’ll want to monitor baseline shifts + regression alerts.

Paula Mendes: yep, events stay the same. we just remove them from the experiment assignment gating.

Leila Farouk: rollout suggestion: ship always-on at 100% but keep a quick kill switch just in case (config-level disable). we’ve been burned before.

Dylan Brooks: we can keep the server-side config disable (no user cohort). basically “always-on” but reversible.

Marissa Cole: action items:
- Kenji: updated copy for #4 + small spec in thread
- Dylan/Jada: update config list + targeting (10k tokens threshold) + keep kill switch
- Paula/Logan: confirm event coverage notes for streaming + add to follow-on backlog
- Ben: incorporate decision into sprint readout

Kenji Nakamura: copy for #4 (draft):
Title: “See your usage so far”
Body: “Track tokens, latency, and errors as you iterate.”
CTA: “Open usage dashboard”
Alt title if we want more concrete: “What did that request cost?”

Soojin Lee: prefer “What did that request cost?” for developers. but maybe soften: “What did that request cost (in tokens)?”

Ben Carter: +1 to the concrete one. we saw in emails that “cost in tokens” language gets clicks.

Marissa Cole: cool. let’s go with:
Title: “What did that request cost (in tokens)?”
Body: “See tokens + latency breakdowns to optimize quickly.”
CTA: “Open usage dashboard”

Dylan Brooks: ack. will update config today and aim to deploy tomorrow morning PST.

Jada Williams: I’ll wire the new targeting rule (first_success=true AND tokens_consumed_total>=10000) and keep `dismissed_at` logic the same.

Leila Farouk: once it’s in staging, tag me and I’ll do a quick pass on dismissal + org switching.

Marissa Cole: thanks all. locking decision as above.
